title: Board the last wooden whaleship at Mystic Seaport
description: The Charles W Morgan, launched 1841, is the only wooden whaleship left afloat anywhere. The yard around her still builds and repairs by hand.

title: See the Gutenberg Bible at the Beinecke
description: Walls of translucent marble filter daylight onto a glass tower of books six storeys high. Free, and one of the strangest interiors in the country.

title: Drive the Litchfield Hills in October
description: White clapboard greens and covered bridges through the north-west corner, close enough to New York that people forget it is quiet.

title: See where Mark Twain wrote Huckleberry Finn
description: A nineteen-room Gothic house he designed himself and went bankrupt keeping. Harriet Beecher Stowe lived next door.

title: Take the boat around the Thimble Islands
description: An archipelago of pink granite outcrops off Stony Creek, some holding a single house, quarried for the stone in Grand Central Station.

title: Walk the Appalachian Trail along the Housatonic
description: The longest riverwalk section of the entire Appalachian Trail runs flat beside the water here for about eight kilometres. Free.

title: Watch the Coast Guard barque Eagle come in
description: A 1936 German-built square rigger taken as war reparations, still the training ship, and open to visitors when she is alongside.

title: Eat oysters where they are dredged
description: Long Island Sound oysters are farmed on beds worked since the 1800s, and the boats land at the same dock the restaurants sit on.

title: Walk the Rehoboth boardwalk out of season
description: A mile of boards, free, and in October the summer crowds are gone but the fudge shops are still open.

title: Cycle Cape Henlopen to the point
description: Second World War observation towers still stand in the dunes, built to spot U-boats off the Delaware Bay.

title: See the du Pont gardens at Longwood
description: A thousand acres of designed landscape around a house holding ninety thousand pieces of American decorative art.

title: Stand on the Green where Delaware ratified first
description: On 7 December 1787 Delaware became the first state, which is why the number one is on the number plates. The Green is unchanged and free.

title: Watch the shorebird migration at Bombay Hook
description: Tidal salt marsh on the Atlantic flyway, with a twelve-mile driving loop and hundreds of thousands of birds passing through in spring.

title: Paddle the Nanticoke River cypress swamp
description: The northernmost stand of bald cypress in the country, paddled between trunks in water the colour of tea.

title: Ride the Wilmington and Western steam train
description: A volunteer-run 1872 branch line through the Red Clay Valley, pulled by steam on scheduled weekends.

title: Eat scrapple for breakfast without flinching
description: Pork scraps and cornmeal, sliced and fried until the edges go crisp. A Mid-Atlantic breakfast that people either grew up with or refuse.

title: Kiss the bricks at the Indianapolis Motor Speedway
description: A metre of the original 1909 brick surface is left at the start-finish line, and winners kiss it. The track tour drives you round it.

title: Climb Mount Baldy at Indiana Dunes
description: A moving sand dune on the Lake Michigan shore with a steel mill on one horizon and Chicago on the other.

title: Walk Brown County State Park in October
description: The largest state park in Indiana, in hills the glaciers missed, and the best autumn colour in the Midwest outside New England.

title: Walk the modernist architecture of Columbus
description: A town of 50,000 with buildings by Saarinen, Pei and Roche, because one local industrialist paid the architects' fees for four decades.

title: Go underground at Marengo Cave
description: Found in 1883 by two children who climbed down a sinkhole with a candle. A national landmark, and still privately run.

title: Cycle the Pufferbelly and Rivergreenway trails
description: Forty kilometres of free path along three rivers through the middle of the city.

title: Watch the Little 500 bike race
description: Two hundred laps on a cinder track by student teams on identical single-speed bikes, run since 1951 and the reason Breaking Away exists.

title: Buy pie in northern Indiana Amish country
description: One of the largest Amish settlements in the country, with a Tuesday auction that has run since 1922 and buggies on the road shoulder.

title: Ride the Fenelon Place elevator
description: Ninety metres of cable car up a bluff, built in 1882 by a banker who wanted to get home for lunch. Three states visible at the top.

title: Drive the Loess Hills scenic byway
description: Wind-blown silt piled into hills up to sixty metres deep, a landform found at this scale in only one other place on earth, in China.

title: Find the covered bridges of Madison County
description: Six of the original nineteen survive, roofed to protect the timber trusses rather than the travellers. Free to visit, all of them.

title: Walk the bear and bird mounds above the Mississippi
description: Two hundred earthworks built between 1400 and 750 years ago, some shaped like animals and only readable from the bluff above.

title: Eat your way through the Iowa State Fair
description: The butter cow has been sculpted every year since 1911. Around eighty foods are sold on a stick, which is the point.

title: Walk the Amana Colonies
description: Seven villages founded in 1855 by German pietists who held everything in common until 1932, and still make the furniture and the wine.

title: Swim in the Iowa Great Lakes
description: One of only three blue-water glacial lakes in the world by the local reckoning, and where the whole state seems to go in July.

title: See the tulips at Pella in May
description: Three hundred thousand bulbs and a working Dutch windmill, in a town settled by Dutch dissenters in 1847.

title: Drive the Flint Hills Scenic Byway
description: The last large stand of tallgrass prairie on earth, saved because the ground is too rocky to plough. In June the grass is over your head.

title: Walk the Tallgrass Prairie National Preserve
description: Four thousand hectares with a bison herd, a stone barn from 1881, and nothing on the horizon in any direction. Free.

title: See the Garden of Eden folk art at Lucas
description: A Civil War veteran spent twenty-two years covering his log-cabin plot in concrete sculpture about labour and capital. He is buried in it.

title: Stand under Monument Rocks on the high plains
description: Chalk pillars twenty metres high left by an inland sea, on private land the owners let people visit free, down eight kilometres of dirt road.

title: Walk Boot Hill and the Santa Fe Trail ruts
description: Wagon ruts from the Santa Fe Trail are still visible west of town, cut deep enough by 1870 to survive a century and a half of weather.

title: Cycle the Arkansas River path in Wichita
description: Free paved path along both banks, past the Keeper of the Plains sculpture where the two rivers meet and fire pots are lit at dusk.

title: See real Mercury and Apollo hardware at the Cosmosphere
description: Hutchinson holds the largest collection of Russian space artefacts outside Moscow, and the actual Apollo 13 command module.

title: Eat steak at the Grand Central Hotel
description: Flint Hills beef eaten in the county it was raised in, on a brick main street ending at a French-roofed courthouse from 1873.

title: Eat crab with a mallet and Old Bay
description: Blue crab steamed and tipped onto brown paper. You are given a mallet and no cutlery, and it takes about three hours to eat properly.

title: See the wild ponies on Assateague Island
description: A feral herd on a barrier island, managed by fence into a Maryland group and a Virginia group. Camping here means securing your food properly.

title: Walk the Naval Academy and the state house
description: The oldest state house still in legislative use, where Washington resigned his commission in 1783. The dome is loblolly pine, no nails.

title: Sail a skipjack on the Chesapeake
description: The last commercial sailing fleet in North America, still dredging oysters under sail because the law requires it on certain days.

title: Cycle the Great Allegheny Passage
description: Two hundred and forty kilometres of former railway, joining the C&O towpath so you can ride from Pittsburgh to Washington without a road.

title: Ski or paddle at Deep Creek Lake
description: Western Maryland is high enough for real snow, so the same lake is a ski weekend in February and a swimming one in July.

title: Look for shark teeth under Calvert Cliffs
description: Miocene cliffs eroding into the bay, shedding fossil teeth onto the beach after every storm. A two-mile walk in from the car park.

title: Walk the Antietam battlefield at dawn
description: The bloodiest single day in American history, 17 September 1862. The farmland is kept as it was, which is what makes it land.

title: Watch half a million sandhill cranes on the Platte
description: Eighty per cent of the world's sandhill cranes stop on eighty kilometres of river each March. From a blind at dawn it is deafening.

title: See Carhenge
description: Stonehenge built from thirty-nine grey-painted American cars in 1987 as a memorial to the builder's father. Free, and open always.

title: Walk to the top of Scotts Bluff
description: A landmark on the Oregon Trail visible for a day's travel in either direction. Wagon ruts are still cut into the ground below it.

title: Drive the Sandhills Journey byway
description: Fifty thousand square kilometres of grass-stabilised dune, the largest such formation in the western hemisphere, and almost nobody on the road.

title: Walk the badlands at Toadstool Geologic Park
description: Mushroom-shaped rock in dry badlands, with a mammoth-kill site nearby and a campground of eight spots and no water.

title: See the big cats at Henry Doorly Zoo
description: The largest indoor desert and the largest indoor rainforest in the world, in a city that keeps quietly funding it.

title: See Chimney Rock from the trail route
description: The most mentioned landmark in overland trail diaries. It has eroded measurably since, so what you see is smaller than what they described.

title: Tank the Niobrara River
description: Floating a stretch of river in a livestock tank is a genuine Nebraska tradition, past two hundred waterfalls falling off the valley side.

title: Watch the autumn raptor migration at Cape May
description: The peninsula funnels migrating birds to its tip before they cross the bay. On a good September day the hawk count runs into thousands.

title: Paddle the cedar water of the Pine Barrens
description: Four thousand square kilometres of pine forest over an aquifer, with water stained red by cedar and iron, an hour from Philadelphia.

title: See a band at the Stone Pony
description: Open since 1974 and still a working room rather than a shrine, on a boardwalk that has been derelict and rebuilt twice since.

title: Walk to Mount Tammany at the Water Gap
description: A steep red-dot climb to a view straight down the notch the river cut through the ridge. Free, busy at weekends, worth an early start.

title: Cycle the Delaware and Raritan Canal towpath
description: Seventy kilometres of flat gravel towpath from Trenton to New Brunswick, past locks still worked by hand for the water supply.

title: Walk the Absecon Lighthouse and the boardwalk
description: Two hundred and twenty-eight steps up the tallest lighthouse in New Jersey, built in 1857 after a run of wrecks on the bar.

title: Eat a pork roll and look at Manhattan
description: The state argues about whether it is pork roll or Taylor ham depending on which half you are in. The skyline view is free either way.

title: Walk the undeveloped dunes at Island Beach
description: Sixteen kilometres of barrier island left as it was, with ospreys nesting and a maritime forest behind the primary dune.

title: Sit at the Oklahoma City National Memorial
description: One hundred and sixty-eight empty chairs, one for each person killed on 19 April 1995, nineteen of them small. The reflecting pool is free to visit.

title: Look for bison in the Wichita Mountains
description: Granite hills full of free-roaming bison, elk and longhorn, on one of the oldest refuges in the country. Free entry.

title: Walk the art deco of downtown Tulsa
description: Oil money built one of the densest collections of art deco in America between 1920 and 1935, and most of it is still standing.

title: Understand the Greenwood massacre where it happened
description: Black Wall Street was destroyed from the air and by mob over two days in 1921. The rebuilt district now carries the history openly.

title: Follow Route 66 across Oklahoma
description: More original alignment survives here than in any other state, including a stretch of the 1926 nine-foot-wide Ribbon Road.

title: Swim in the Beavers Bend clearwater
description: Cold clear water released from the bottom of a dam, in pine forest that feels like Arkansas rather than the plains.

title: Stand on Black Mesa, the highest point in Oklahoma
description: A lava-capped mesa at 1,516 metres in the far panhandle, thirteen kilometres return, with dinosaur tracks in the valley below.

title: Walk the Tallgrass Prairie Preserve at Pawhuska
description: Nineteen thousand hectares of restored prairie on the Osage Nation with around two thousand bison. Free, and the road through is gravel.
